examples.en: I eat rice with kidney beans mixed in.
The kidney beans sprouted, so I planted them in a pot.

examples.ko: 초등학교 때 강낭콩 키우기 숙제가 있었어요.
examples.en: In elementary school we had homework growing kidney beans.
Boiled kidney beans taste good in a salad.
I made soup with kidney beans.
Kidney beans are also rich in protein.

explain: 밥에 섞어 먹거나 수프, 샐러드에 넣는 콩이에요. 팥이나 완두콩과는 다른 콩이고, 학교에서 식물을 관찰할 때 키우는 콩으로도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a bean eaten mixed into rice or added to soup and salad. It is different from red beans and green peas, and it often appears as the bean children grow when observing plants at school.

examples.en: The government builds a new bridge.
That company constructed apartments.
They are looking for land to build a factory.
They are building a park in the city.
It took three years to build.
They built a road, and the village became more convenient.

explain: '짓다'는 집이나 건물을 일상적으로 말할 때 쓰고, '건설하다'는 다리, 도로, 댐, 도시처럼 큰 것을 지을 때 써요. '나라를 건설하다'처럼 사회나 나라를 세운다는 뜻으로도 써요. '건설 회사', '건설 현장'이 자주 쓰여요.
explain_en: The everyday verb for building houses is used casually, while this one fits big things such as bridges, roads, dams and cities. It can also mean founding a nation or society. Construction company and construction site are common phrases.

dis.h: build big works like roads or bridges

p.n: 가설하다 means erecting or laying a structure across a gap.

examples.en: The snow that piled up all winter has finally melted.

examples.ko: 저는 겨우내 감기 한 번 안 걸렸어요.
examples.en: I didn't catch a cold even once all winter.
Bears sleep in their dens all winter long.

examples.ko: 겨우내 입던 두꺼운 외투를 세탁소에 맡겼어요.
examples.en: I left the thick coat I wore all winter at the dry cleaner's.
Grandmother knitted in her room all winter.

examples.ko: 겨우내 얼어 있던 강물이 풀리기 시작해요.
examples.en: The river that stayed frozen all winter is starting to thaw.

explain: '겨울 내내'와 뜻이 같지만 한 낱말처럼 바로 동사 앞에 써요. '겨울 내내'보다 짧고 글에서 자주 보여요. 봄을 기다리는 느낌이 있어서 눈이 녹거나 봄이 오는 이야기와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It means the same as '겨울 내내' but works as one word placed directly before a verb. It is shorter than '겨울 내내' and common in writing. It carries a feeling of waiting for spring, so it fits stories about snow melting or spring arriving.

examples.en: My father retired and returned to his hometown to farm.

examples.ko: 도시에서 일하다가 귀농하는 사람이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More people are leaving city jobs to take up farming.
I'm thinking of going back to farming later.
I started apple farming after returning to the countryside.

examples.ko: 그 부부는 귀농한 지 삼 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been three years since that couple moved to the countryside to farm.

examples.ko: 귀농하려면 먼저 땅과 집을 알아봐야 해요.
examples.en: To start farming in the country, you first need to look for land and a house.

explain: '귀농하다'는 도시에서 살다가 농사를 지으러 농촌으로 가는 거예요. 농촌으로 이사해서 농사를 하지 않고 사는 것은 '귀촌하다'라고 해서 달라요. 기사에서는 '귀농 귀촌'으로 함께 자주 써요.
explain_en: '귀농하다' is leaving the city to farm in the countryside. Moving to the countryside without farming is '귀촌하다', which is different. In news the two are often written together as '귀농 귀촌'.

examples.en: In spring we make soybean paste soup with shepherd's purse.
Grandmother dug up shepherd's purse in the field and brought it.

examples.ko: 냉이는 향이 강해서 처음엔 낯설 수 있어요.
examples.en: Its scent is strong, so it may feel unfamiliar at first.
Shepherd's purse is already out at the market.
I blanched the greens and mixed them with red pepper paste.

examples.ko: 봄이 되면 냉이랑 달래 생각이 나요.
examples.en: When spring comes, I think of shepherd's purse and wild chives.

explain: 봄을 알리는 나물이라서 3월 즈음 시장에 많이 나와요. 된장국이나 무침으로 먹고, 뿌리까지 같이 먹는 게 특징이에요. 비슷한 봄나물로 '달래'와 '쑥'이 있어요. '냉이를 캐다', '냉이를 무치다'처럼 동사와 같이 외워요.
explain_en: It is a spring herald, widely sold around March. People eat it in soybean paste soup or as a seasoned side dish, roots included. Other spring greens are '달래' and '쑥'. Learn it with '냉이를 캐다' and '냉이를 무치다'.

examples.en: Add water to the flour and slowly knead it.
My mother kneaded the flour to make kalguksu noodles.

examples.ko: 빵을 반죽하는 일은 생각보다 힘이 들어요.
examples.en: Kneading bread dough takes more effort than I thought.

examples.ko: 먼저 계란을 넣고 반죽한 다음 십 분 동안 쉬게 하세요.
examples.en: First add an egg and knead, then let it rest for ten minutes.
I made dough with the kids and baked cookies.

examples.ko: 너무 오래 반죽하면 빵이 딱딱해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you knead too long, the bread can turn hard.

explain: 밀가루나 쌀가루에 물을 섞어 손으로 뭉치는 일이에요. 명사 '반죽'은 그렇게 만든 덩어리를 가리켜서 '반죽을 만들다', '반죽이 질다'처럼 써요. 섞는 것만 말할 때는 '섞다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means mixing flour or rice flour with water and working it into a lump by hand. The noun 반죽 is that lump itself, as in 반죽을 만들다 and 반죽이 질다. For just mixing, say 섞다.

en: to fire; to launch; to set off

examples.en: Scientists launch a rocket.
The company launched a satellite.
They set off fireworks at the end of the festival.
The plan is to launch the spacecraft tomorrow.
The place where they launched the rocket is by the sea.
They run a check before launching.

explain: 쏘아 올리는 사람이나 기관이 주어예요. '쏘다'와 달리 로켓, 위성, 불꽃처럼 큰 것을 올릴 때 많이 써요. 활이나 총에는 '쏘다'를 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: The subject is the person or organization doing the launching. Unlike plain '쏘다', it is used often for big equipment like rockets, satellites and fireworks. For arrows and guns, people say '쏘다' more often.

examples.en: On Easter, churches hand out eggs.

examples.ko: 부활절은 해마다 날짜가 달라서 달력을 확인해요.
examples.en: Easter falls on a different date every year, so I check the calendar.
On Easter morning I attended a service with my family.
My friend decorated the Easter eggs beautifully.
After Easter the weather gets warm.

examples.ko: 해외에서는 부활절 연휴에 여행 가는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Abroad, many people travel over the Easter holiday.

explain: 기독교에서 예수의 부활을 기념하는 날이에요. 한국에서는 공휴일이 아니라서 쉬는 날은 아니고 교회 행사로 지내요. 크리스마스와 달리 날짜가 해마다 바뀌고 항상 일요일이에요.
explain_en: It is the Christian day marking the resurrection of Jesus. In Korea it is not a public holiday, so it is observed mainly through church events. Unlike Christmas, the date changes every year and always falls on a Sunday.

examples.en: It's the weekend, so the market is bustling with people.

examples.ko: 명절에는 기차역이 늘 북적대서 표 구하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The train station is always crowded during holidays, so it is hard to get tickets.

examples.ko: 식당 앞이 줄 선 사람들로 북적대고 있어요.
examples.en: The area in front of the restaurant is crowded with people in line.
The bustling noise from next door woke me up.
The library is not crowded on weekday afternoons.
It's a holiday, so what do we do if the airport is packed?

explain: 사람이 많이 모여서 복잡하고 시끌시끌한 모습이에요. '북적거리다'도 같은 뜻이에요. '붐비다'는 사람이 많아 복잡하다는 점이 중심이고, '북적대다'는 활기나 소란스러운 느낌도 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a place full of people, busy and noisy. '북적거리다' means the same thing. '붐비다' focuses on being crowded, while '북적대다' also carries a feeling of liveliness or noise.

examples.ko: 아버지는 이십 년 동안 선원으로 일하셨어요.
examples.en: My father worked as a sailor for twenty years.
The crew members are tidying the nets on the ship.

examples.ko: 폭풍이 오자 선원이 모두 갑판에 모였어요.
examples.en: When the storm came, all the sailors gathered on deck.

examples.ko: 이 배는 선원 서른 명을 태우고 출발해요.
examples.en: This ship departs carrying thirty crew members.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때 선원이 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I wanted to be a sailor.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 실종된 선원을 찾고 있다고 했어요.
examples.en: The news said they were searching for the missing crew member.

explain: 선원은 배에서 일하는 사람 전체를 가리켜요. 선장도 선원에 포함되고, 선장과 구별해서 말할 때는 '선장과 선원'이라고 해요. 군대의 '해군'이나 놀러 타는 사람 '승객'과는 달라요.
explain_en: 선원 refers to everyone who works on a ship. The captain is also included, but to distinguish them Koreans say '선장과 선원'. It differs from '해군' (navy) and '승객' (passenger).

examples.en: That man picked pockets on the subway yesterday.
He got caught by the police while picking pockets at the market.

examples.ko: 소매치기하는 사람은 보통 눈에 잘 안 띄어요.
examples.en: People who pick pockets usually don't stand out.

examples.ko: 저를 소매치기한 사람은 아직 못 찾았어요.
examples.en: They still haven't found the person who picked my pocket.

examples.ko: 그는 어렸을 때 소매치기하며 살았다고 말했어요.
examples.en: He said he lived by picking pockets when he was young.
The culprit picked the tourist's wallet and ran away.

explain: 피해자 입장에서는 '소매치기를 당하다'가 자연스러워요. '소매치기하다'는 저지른 사람을 말할 때 써요. 훔치는 일 전체는 '훔치다'라고 해요.
explain_en: From the victim's side, 소매치기를 당하다 is the natural phrase. 소매치기하다 is used about the person who did it. Stealing in general is 훔치다.

examples.ko: 승선 시간은 출발 한 시간 전부터예요.
examples.en: Boarding time starts one hour before departure.
You must check your ID before boarding the ship.
When boarding began, people lined up.

examples.ko: 승선 표를 보여 주면 배에 탈 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you show your boarding pass, you can get on the ship.
You can board only after receiving safety training.

examples.ko: 승선 방법은 안내 방송으로 알려 줘요.
examples.en: They announce how to board over the speaker.

explain: 배에 타는 일을 말하는 공식적인 말이에요. 반대말은 '하선'이에요. 일상에서는 '배를 타다'라고 하고, '승선'은 선착장 안내나 뉴스에서 보여요.
explain_en: A formal word for getting on a ship. The opposite is '하선'. In daily life you say '배를 타다'; '승선' appears in terminal notices and news.

en: the first day of a month

examples.en: On the first day of the lunar month, my grandmother goes to the temple.
Seollal is the first day of the first lunar month.
The first day of this month is a Monday.
From the new moon to the full moon, the moon gradually gets bigger.
When the first of the month comes, I hang a new calendar.
My grandmother goes to the temple on every first day and full moon day.

explain: 한 달의 첫째 날이에요. 일상에서는 '1일'이라고 하고, 음력 이야기나 명절, 전통 행사에서 자주 나와요. 짝으로 '보름'(15일), '그믐'(마지막 날)을 알아 두세요.
explain_en: It means the first day of a month. In everyday talk people just say '1일', while '초하루' often appears in talk about the lunar calendar, holidays and traditional events. Also learn the related words '보름' (the 15th) and '그믐' (the last day).

en: to be released; to be discharged

examples.en: He is released from prison this month.

examples.ko: 오 년 만에 출소한 남자가 인터뷰를 했어요.
examples.en: A man released after five years gave an interview.
He says he wants to live with his family once he's released.
It's hard to find a job after being released.
The news said he's due to be released tomorrow.
My brother was released, so the family went to meet him.

explain: 교도소에서 형을 마치고 나오는 것을 말해요. 반대말은 '수감되다'예요. 주로 뉴스에서 많이 나오는 말이고, 일상 대화에서는 조심해서 써요.
explain_en: It means leaving prison after serving a sentence; the opposite is 수감되다 (be imprisoned). You mostly hear it in the news, and people are careful about using it in casual talk.

examples.en: On my day off, I read books for half the day.
Preparing for the move took half a day.

examples.ko: 한나절이면 이 일을 끝낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can finish this job in half a day.
There was no contact for half a day, so I was worried.

examples.ko: 한나절쯤 걸으면 산 정상에 닿을 거예요.
examples.en: If you walk for about half a day, you will reach the summit.

examples.ko: 아무 소득 없는 회의로 한나절을 그냥 보냈어요.
examples.en: I wasted half a day on a pointless meeting.

explain: 하루의 절반쯤 되는 시간으로, 주로 낮 동안을 말해요. '반나절'과 비슷한 뜻으로 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 시간이 꽤 걸렸다는 느낌을 줄 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is about half of a day, mainly during daytime hours. It is often used much like '반나절'. It fits well when you want to say something took quite a while.
